commit_message:
avcodec/sanm: better frame size detection for old codecs

The size of the video frame (FOBJ) of the old codecs (ANIMv0/1/2) can
very reliably be determined:
- ANIMv0/1 (=Rebel Assault 1) uses a 384x242 internal buffer for
  everything.  The codec parameters only describe the size and offset
  of the specific FOBJ on that buffer.
- ANIMv2 titles usually use one of the fullscreen codecs (37/47/48)
  as first FOBJ, and their dimensions can generally be trusted.
- RA2 uses 424x260 as internal buffer, use that if encountered:
  08PLAY.SAN does not use codec37 so we need to guess using the
  codec coordinates.
- ignore sizes smaller than 2x2 or larger than 800x600.
- some game videos have an initial fobj with either 1x1 or -1x-1
  pixels in size, ignore them with a warning (Full Throttle
  and the Rebel Assault 2 xxRETRY.SAN videos).

Once a known/valid dimension set has been discovered, use it and
don't change it for subsequent FOBJs, rather clamp the large frame
to the determined dimensions.

Tested with RA1, RA2, Full Throttle, Dig, Outlaws, SotE and MotS
videos.

Signed-off-by: Manuel Lauss <manuel.lauss@gmail.com>

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/sanm: Check w, h for subversion < 2

Fixes: 410609432/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_SANM_fuzzer-4935159201988608
Fixes: out of array access

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Reviewed-by: Manuel Lauss <manuel.lauss@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 3afae0f4409a on top of intro 93b0ca26acb9 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): In FFmpeg's SANM/ANIM decoder (libavcodec/sanm.c), process_frame_obj() determines the internal decode buffer size the first time a frame object (FOBJ) is processed. For old-format files where ctx->subversion < 2 (Rebel Assault 1 ANIMv0/1), the code unconditionally assumes and hard-codes a fixed internal buffer size of 384x242 pixels and immediately marks ctx->have_dimensions = 1, without verifying that the FOBJ's actual parsed width/height (which can range up to 800x600 per the earlier generic sanity check) actually fit inside that fixed 384x242 buffer. Because the allocated/initialized buffers are sized to 384x242 (via init_sizes/init_buffers), but downstream codec routines use the attacker-controlled, larger w/h/left/top values to index into the buffer, a crafted file can trigger out-of-bounds array accesses. Root cause: The frame-size detection logic added in commit 93b0ca26ac ("better frame size detection for old codecs") assumes that for old ANIMv0/1 (subversion < 2) files the internal frame is always exactly 384x242, and unconditionally trusts this fixed size without cross-checking it against the actually parsed FOBJ w/h fields, which are only bounded by a much looser generic check (w<=800, h<=600). This allows fields not fitting the assumed fixed buffer to pass through.
